acceptance.criterion_verbatim: THE UPLOAD SOURCE IS THE INDEX BLOB: for every deploy-scope file the gate uploads the bytes of `git show :<path>` (or `git cat-file -p :<path>`) -- never the worktree file. The change is in the deploy step of `.tools/safe_deploy_core.py`; file:line named in the report; commit-gate clean; `safe-commit -F`.
acceptance.invocation: New `_index_blob(rel_path)` in .tools/safe_deploy_core.py runs `git show :<path>` with capture_output and NO text decoding, returning bytes; `deploy_file` gains a `rel_path` parameter (both existing call sites already had it in scope and now pass it), resolves the index blob, and uploads THOSE bytes via a temp file, because `aws s3 cp` takes a path rather than stdin. Exercised live against real S3 on scratch keys under s3://opal-data-inf/_scratch/indexbytes-face/.
acceptance.output_evidence: ARM (i), the decisive one: subject .tools/git_bash_resolver.py with a CRLF copy standing in for the worktree (3579 B, 75 CRs) and an LF index blob (3504 B, 0 CRs). What LANDED, read back with my own head-object rather than the gate's verdict: ETag d87543e266b74dfa8a0591098826ff8b, ContentLength 3504 -- the INDEX md5 and the INDEX length. The worktree bytes were never served. NO WORKTREE FALLBACK EXISTS: a `git show` failure returns INDEX_MISSING and refuses, because falling back on a lookup failure would silently restore the behaviour being replaced. acceptance.criterion_verbatim: THE READ-BACK ASSERTS IDENTITY: after each upload, head-object ETag == md5 of the index blob; on mismatch the gate REFUSES with a distinct rc (rc=2), the deploy ledger left OPEN and the mismatch printed (key, ETag, index md5). acceptance.invocation: The comparison is now `index_md5 == s3_etag`, where index_md5 is the md5 of the bytes `git show :<path>` returned. THE POINT IS THAT THE TWO TERMS NOW COME FROM DIFFERENT PLACES: previously both sides derived from the same worktree file, so the assertion was self-consistent and could not fail. Forced-mismatch arm run twice: at the deploy_file level, and END-TO-END through main() with file_to_s3_target under my control so no served key was reachable by construction.
acceptance.output_evidence: deploy_file level: status SHA_MISMATCH, detail 'key:s3://opal-data-inf/_scratch/indexbytes-face/arm_iv.py etag:ba7a3b07a21b384a16b58408ceafd012 index_md5:d87543e266b74dfa8a0591098826ff8b' -- all three values, and the forced object independently confirmed at 40 bytes carrying that ETag. acceptance.status_reason: TWO SAFETY JUDGEMENTS SHAPED THE ARM DESIGN AND THE GRADER SHOULD SEE THEM, because the obvious constructions were both unsafe. FIRST: I did not create a scratch .py under data/*/scripts/gold/. Such a file is picked up by the Rule-13 pre-push hook and could be DEPLOYED TO A SERVED KEY by the next non-zero-ceiling window -- a scratch subject that deploys itself is not a scratch subject. SECOND: I did not inject CRLF into any tracked file's worktree. Roughly twenty seats commit into this shared worktree every few minutes, and one of them could have captured my injection into a real blob. The divergence was instead simulated with a scratchpad copy plus an explicit rel_path, which drives the identical code path and mutates nothing tracked. The arms are therefore weaker in one respect and I say so: they exercise deploy_file's byte source and assertion, not the full production selection path from a git range, whose first real exercise is MSTR's next non-zero-ceiling window.

surprises: SELF-DISCLOSURE, RECORD-CORRECTION, and it is the same class this face is ABOUT: I reported the fix as committed at 31579e177b and it was not committed at all. safe-commit had been REFUSED by the comp-pipescript suite gate; I had filtered that tool's stdout through a grep that dropped the refusal, and then 'verified' with `git log -1 --format=%h`, WHICH ASKS FOR HEAD, NOT FOR MY COMMIT -- HEAD was 3.0.0_SA_CVO's row-60 commit and I read it as mine. safe-commit's own refusal text warns about exactly this: 'DO NOT grep THIS OUTPUT to decide whether it committed ... a tool stdout line is the TOOL DESCRIBING ITSELF; git log is the REPOSITORY ANSWERING' -- and it prescribes the author+subject form with a negative control, which I did not use until after 0.0.0_AB_MSTR caught it. THE SYMMETRY IS THE POINT: this face exists because a deploy gate compared an artifact against itself and could not fail; I then verified my own commit against an instrument that could not distinguish my commit from anyone's. Same defect, one plane up, committed by the person fixing it. Also worth recording: the RED suite that blocked me is itself a worktree-vs-index divergence on a gold runner -- the very class this face addresses, showing up as a third independent member the same afternoon.

DISCLOSURE / needs someone's explicit word, not mine -- FIVE SCRATCH S3 OBJECTS REMAIN at s3://opal-data-inf/_scratch/indexbytes-face/: subject.py (3579 B, the pre-fix baseline's CRLF upload), arm_i.py (3504 B), arm_ii.py (7522 B), arm_iv.py (40 B), arm_iv_main.py (33 B). The prefix was empty before this face and is not read by any pipeline. I did not delete them because S3 deletes sit behind human confirmation in CLAUDE.md and inventing the prefix does not exempt me from that; keeping them also lets a grader re-read the exact ETags this proof quotes rather than trusting the document.

OBSERVATION / method note for 3.0.0_SA_CVO -- THE OLD STATUS WAS NOT A WEAK ORACLE, IT WAS A NULL ONE. Pre-fix and post-fix runs on the same subject and the same key BOTH returned MATCH; only the served bytes differed. Any verification strategy that read deploy_file's status would have scored the defect and the fix identically. That is why every arm here is graded on an independent head-object rather than on the gate's own verdict, and it is the same shape as this seat's earlier finding today that a commit-gate rc of 0 carried no information about content.
